title: Senior's toolkit: everyday power tools
summary: History views, ranges, recovering shared branches, stacks, rerere and line endings, with the flags that matter.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: everyday power tools
steps.body: The commands that turn a scary Git morning into a two-minute fix. Each one is read-only or easy to undo when used as shown.

toolkit.what: The whole repository as a drawing: every branch, tag and remote-tracking ref, and where they fork and join.
flags: only the main line through merges
toolkit.when: before any merge, rebase or review

toolkit.what: A file as it was at any commit or tag, without checking anything out.
flags: what one commit changed, files only

toolkit.what: Which server branches already have a commit. `git tag --contains` gives the releases.
flags: branches whose tip is (not) in the current branch

toolkit.what: Check out a remote branch under the same name, tracking it. Use `-c name --track origin/x` to be explicit.
Compares two versions of a commit series commit by commit: what changed in a force-pushed branch.
flags: your rewrite against what is pushed
a teammate's force-push, before against after
toolkit.when: a PR was force-pushed since your review

toolkit.what: Replays only the commits after `<old>` onto `<new>`: the precise tool when a base was squashed or rewritten.
flags: move every branch in a stack along
find `<old>` from the upstream's reflog (default with an upstream)
toolkit.when: a shared branch was force-pushed under your commits

toolkit.what: Rebases the top of a stack and moves every branch inside it.
flags: fold fixups into lower PRs at the same time

toolkit.what: Git remembers each conflict resolution you commit and replays it when the same conflict appears again.
toolkit.when: long rebases, the same fix on several release branches

toolkit.what: After adding `.gitattributes`, rewrites committed files with the right line endings.
flags: what is stored (i/) and on disk (w/)
toolkit.when: every line shows as changed, or `^M: bad interpreter`

steps.prompt: Match each command to the question it answers.
pairs: Which server branches already have this fix?
What did my rewrite change compared with what reviewers saw?
What did this file look like in the release?
Which files are stored with CRLF?
How do all the branches relate right now?

steps.prompt: `git status` says your shared branch and `origin/feature/x` *have diverged, 3 and 1 different commits each*. You did not rewrite anything, and `git log origin/feature/x..feature/x` shows two of a teammate's old commits and one of yours. What do you run?
steps.explain: Your one commit must survive, the teammate's old ones must not come back. A merge would bring them back; a reset would lose yours; a force-push would undo their rewrite on the server.

steps.prompt: Stop CRLF from reaching the repository again, then fix the files already committed.

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Look before you move: `git log --oneline --graph --all` before every rebase or merge, `git range-diff` after every force-push you receive, and `git branch backup` before anything you are not sure about. Turn on `rerere.enabled`, `rebase.updateRefs` and `fetch.prune` once, globally, and commit a `.gitattributes` in every new repository.
